fr.elements: Main Residence; Pool Area; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain; Scattered Vegetation; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to make the single access point visible at night or in reduced visibility conditions.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence large enough for emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the access drive free of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can reach the residence without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for wide emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and move around it without obstruction.
• Mark or identify the pool area with a visible indicator at the perimeter fence so responders are aware of its location during nighttime or low-visibility operations.
• Keep perimeter fence gates unlocked or secured with a single padlock to allow responders to move between areas without delay.
• Thin scattered vegetation in open terrain areas that could slow or block responder movement between the residence and detached structure.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the locations of the main residence, detached structure, pool area, and any locked gates to help responders orient quickly on arrival.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Irrigated Landscape; Long Driveway; Scattered Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang close to or over the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin shrubs scattered near the house to create open gaps between individual plants.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the house to reduce the amount of vegetation in that area.
• Clear dead or dry material from within shrub groupings near the house.
• Keep low branches on trees near the house trimmed up from the ground.
• Maintain open spacing between the irrigated landscape plantings and the exterior walls of the house.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, leaf litter, and debris that could block access.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the road, supporting quick access by emergency vehicles.
• Keep shrubs along the driveway trimmed back so they do not narrow the travel lane or reduce visibility.
• Keep the area around any outbuildings or secondary structures clear of shrub growth on all sides.
